title: Tenant thrift hint layer and graceful quant degradation
author: Maya R. Patel
description: Motivation: Tenant workloads show widely varying short-term burstiness which leads to either wasted tokens (over-prefetch) or increased latency (under-prefetch). We need a tenant-aware, low-risk hint layer that provides conservative prefetch recommendations and a graceful quantization degradation path when higher-precision variants are unavailable. This PR introduces a thin runtime hint layer that surfaces tenant cost targets and recent latency/cold-start signals to the prefetch scheduler, plus a compact quantization fallback matrix that lets the serving runtime degrade model precision in controlled steps when capacity or cost policies demand it. Implementation summary: - new runtime component: tenant_thrift_hint_layer - per-tenant hint object persisted in tenant metadata (TTL-driven) - hint sources: recent latency SLO miss rate, recent token spend, and tenant-configured budget bands - scheduler hooks to prefer warm-prefetch when hints indicate thrift mode - quant_fallback matrix: ordered list of quant profiles (fp16 -> int8_opt -> int8_fast -> int4_safe) with per-profile SLO loss estimates and a safe rollback timer - telemetry: new metrics and tags for prefetch_decision, hint_source, quant_fallback_reason, quant_rollforward_attempt - conservative defaults and an opt-in tenant flag: enable_tenant_thrift_hints (false by default) Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag; opt-in enabled for internal benchmark tenants, staged rollout to 5%, 25%, 100% with monitoring windows during each stage. Safety: hints are advisory; the scheduler will not prefetch beyond configured per-tenant burst caps. Quant fallback includes a canary window where output-quality regressions are sampled and evaluated against golden prompt sets; automatic rollback on quality regression above threshold. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-3187) - [x] Unit tests for hint lifecycle and TTL - [x] Integration test against scheduler simulator with synthetic tenant traces - [x] Telemetry fields instrumented - [x] Feature flag gate and migration script - [x] Docs PR stubbed for admin console settings Testing notes: local unit + integration; ran e2e with 50 synthetic tenants for 48h; observed median token-cost reduction of 6% for thrift-mode tenants with <0.2% increase in median latency. Related: follows work in ENG-3011 (batching defaults) and complements tenant-warmstart heuristics.
commits_summary: 7 commits: init tenant thrift hint layer and schema; add scheduler hooks; implement quant_fallback matrix; telemetry instrumentation; feature flag and migration; unit + integration tests; docs stubs
diff_snippets: + func EvaluateTenantHint(tenantID string, signal TenantSignal) Hint { /* TTL logic, merge heuristics */ }

+ quantFallbackProfiles: - name: fp16
  latency_factor: 1.0
  expected_quality_drop: 0.0
- name: int8_opt
  latency_factor: 0.85
  expected_quality_drop: 0.01
+ scheduler hook: if hint.ThriftMode && withinBurstCap { preferPrefetch = true }
review_comments: Diego Vargas: Nice incremental design. Two asks: 1) Can we make the default quant order configurable per-cluster? 2) Add a safety cap so a buggy hint can't trigger massive prefetches?
Maya R. Patel (author): Answered. Made quant profiles cluster-scoped via quant_profiles.yaml and enforced per-tenant burst caps in scheduler. Added unit tests for the cap.
Priya Kannan: Tests look good; request: add a short runbook entry for ops for how to disable for a tenant quickly.
Maya R. Patel: Added docs/admin/tenant_thrift_hints.md with disable steps and feature flag override.
Liam O'Connor: CI flake on telemetry lint; re-ran and green. Approving pending small comments fixed in squash commit.
release_notes: Add tenant thrift hint layer and configurable quantization fallback matrix. Opt-in feature to reduce unit token cost for bursty tenants; disabled by default. Admin can enable per-tenant and configure cluster-level quant order. Includes telemetry and runbook for safe rollback.
notes_for_release_manager: Feature gated. Migration adds tenant metadata table (nullable). Rollout should follow staged plan in PR description; watch metrics redwood.prefetch_decision and redwood.quant_fallback_{reason} and quality regression alerts for canary tenants.
